results.evidence: RotaMate is a small web app for shared houses. You paste the chore part of your house group chat, and RotaMate returns a weekly rota that names who does each task, on which day, and why the split is fair.
results.note: The draft provides a clear description of the application and its overall function.

results.evidence: The problem: in a shared student house, chores are usually agreed in a long group chat. Promises like "I'll take bins this week" get buried under memes, nobody remembers who swapped with whom, and the same two people end up cleaning the kitchen.
results.note: The draft explains the problem of tracking informal chore agreements in group chats.

results.evidence: How the AI works: RotaMate sends the pasted chat to the Gemini API in two steps. The first call extracts every chore commitment, swap, and excuse as structured JSON (person, task, day, source message). The second call proposes a rota from that list.
results.note: The draft details the multi-step AI implementation using the Gemini API.

results.evidence: Demo: the demonstration video walks through one real-looking chat from paste to finished rota in under three minutes: https://youtu.be/rotamate-demo (unlisted, no login needed).
results.note: The draft includes a link and details for a video demonstration.

results.evidence: Source code and setup: the code is public at https://github.com/example/rotamate. The README explains how to run it locally with Node 20 and where to place your own free Gemini API key in a local environment file that is never committed.
results.note: The draft provides source code repository details and setup instructions.
